placements.why: This envelope documents a deployment-pipeline gating decision — a technical release-engineering control over how Meridian ships — and no strata category exists yet in this repo to hold engineering/systems-practice content. Architecture is the org's known top-level category for exactly this kind of material, so it is minted here as the foundational stratum rather than forcing the content into an unrelated category.

placements.title: release shipping moves from trust-based deployment to cryptographically verified provenance gating
placements.frame: what provenance failure or incident is being cited to justify making artifact-signing a mandatory precondition for a release, and how far does that mandate's scope and ownership reach?
placements.why: Quinton's directive (src-1) makes a signed release manifest mandatory before any Meridian deploy ships, and his incident claim (src-2) supplies the concrete provenance failure — two unsigned artifacts reaching staging last quarter — that motivates it. Xena's three decision-record lines (src-3 Gate, src-4 Scope, src-5 Owner) codify the same instrument: the requirement itself, its reach across staging and production, and the accountable owner. All five expressions are facets of one recurring subject — a deploy pipeline instituting signed-provenance gating in response to a concrete integrity gap — that future envelopes (gate exceptions, compliance checks, further incidents, scope changes) will keep feeding, rather than a one-time fact standing alone.
